text:
sam (eng-platform): Heads-up: we need a telemetry schema for the new cost dashboard — specifically cost per 1K tokens and a breakdown of cache / batch savings. Can infra/runtime teams confirm required fields and cardinality?

maya (product): thx. high-level goals: show 1K-token unit cost, % savings from KV cache, % savings from batching, and ability to slice by model, deployment_type, region, and route_policy. Console needs CSV export too.

oliver (eng-runtime): quick q — do you want billed tokens (after prefix/KV caching) or raw tokens emitted by the model? That changes where we instrument.

sam (eng-platform): billed tokens for the primary metric (reflects what we charge). But runtime should emit both raw and billed if possible so data team can recompute.

priya (eng-infra): cardinality warning: model_id + quant_level + region + deployment_type + route_policy + customer_id is a lot. Proposal: required dims = model_id, quant_level, region, deployment_type, route_tier (low/standard/premium). Optional high-card dims collected at sampling rate for top customers.

diego (data): agree. For rollups we can do hourly aggregates. Suggested atomic counters: tokens_before_cache, tokens_after_cache, tokens_billed (after batching/billing logic). For batch-savings: batch_size, batch_tokens_saved.

oliver (eng-runtime): implementation notes from runtime side: we can emit per-request fields and a lightweight per-batch event. Per-request tags: model_id, quant_level, route_policy, had_kv_cache_hit:true/false, request_id. Per-batch event: batch_id, batch_size, total_tokens_before, total_tokens_after. Example metric names we can register:

```
requests.tokens.raw
requests.tokens.after_cache
requests.tokens.billed
requests.cache.hits
batches.count
batches.size.avg
batches.tokens_saved.total
```

maya (product): UX calc for cost-per-1K: (sum(cost_estimate)/sum(billed_tokens)) * 1000. Where cost_estimate ideally comes from infra pricing table applied in ETL, but if runtime can attach a normalized cost_estimate field per-request that's helpful for quick charts.

priya (eng-infra): runtime shouldn't hardcode pricing. We'll maintain a price table and compute cost_estimate downstream. Runtime will emit token counters + a boolean indicating whether a request was served from cache vs fallback. Also: sampling for high-throughput customers (1/s or 1/100) to avoid cardinality blowup.

sam (eng-platform): summary action items: @oliver add per-request metrics: tokens_before_cache, tokens_after_cache, tokens_billed, request_id; add per-batch event: batch_id, batch_size, tokens_saved. @priya confirm allowed tags and sampling policy. @diego produce final rollup SQL + expected schemas. @maya provide console formulas and chart mocks.

oliver (eng-runtime): will prototype payloads and a small patch for emitting batch events today. sample payload (very small):

```
{ request_id: "r_123", model_id: "redwood-7b", quant_level: "int8", region: "us-west1", had_kv_cache_hit: false, tokens_before_cache: 120, tokens_after_cache: 120, tokens_billed: 120 }
{ batch_event: true, batch_id: "b_456", model_id: "redwood-7b", batch_size: 8, total_tokens_before: 960, total_tokens_after: 480, tokens_saved: 480 }
```

telemetry-bot: Reminder: please add new metric names to metrics-catalog before pushing to prod.

diego (data): I'll draft the hourly rollup and a view that produces: total_billed_tokens, total_raw_tokens, total_tokens_saved_by_cache, total_tokens_saved_by_batching, cost_estimate (using infra price table). Will also include derivations for % savings and cost_per_1k. Note: dedupe by request_id to handle retries. Target: share EOD.

maya (product): can we also surface cost-per-1K for canary vs prod? route_policy tag is required for that.

sam (eng-platform): yes — add route_policy to tags. One more ask: make sure model_version and model_family are separate dims for rollups.

priya (eng-infra): noted. I'll confirm sampling rates for public vs enterprise customers and add rate-limited collectors for high-volume customers.

sam (eng-platform): OK let's sync tomorrow 11:30am to finalize schema and registrations. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
